definition: The percentage of the country's population with access to an electricity supply, whether from the grid or from off-grid systems. Use the latest official national figure for the report's fiscal year, sourced from the national statistics office, the most recent census, or the national energy department. Feeds the Access to Electricity KPI. Note that the valid range is 0 to 1, so enter the value as a decimal proportion (for example 0.95 for 95%), and report the national figure rather than coverage within the utility's service area.

The country's air connectivity expressed per 1,000 persons of national population, indicating how well connected the country is by scheduled air services relative to its population size. Derive it from the national air connectivity measure (see IATA Air Connectivity Score) and the latest official national population figure for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Air Connectivity per 1000 People KPI. Ensure the same population vintage is used here as in the Population input so context indicators remain consistent.
synonyms: air transport connectivity per thousand people

definition: The country's air connectivity expressed per unit of gross domestic product (% per unit GDP), indicating how well connected the country is by scheduled air services relative to the size of its economy. Derive it from the national air connectivity measure and the latest official GDP figure published by the national statistics office or central bank for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Air Connectivity per Unit GDP KPI. Take care to use the same GDP vintage as other GDP-based context inputs.
synonyms: air transport connectivity per unit of economic output

definition: The average number of persons per household across the country, expressed in persons per household. Source the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent national census; where no direct figure is published it is the national population divided by the number of households. Feeds the Average Household Size KPI. Use the national figure, not an estimate for the utility's service area only.

A descriptive selection identifying how fuel prices are regulated in the country, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the current national arrangement for setting or controlling the price of fuel (for example regulated by a national authority or set by the market), as at the end of the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Fuel Pricing Regulation KPI. This describes the national fuel-price regime, not the utility's own fuel purchase contracts.

A descriptive selection identifying the country's access to fuel supply, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes how the country obtains its fuel (for example direct import, regional distribution hub, or domestic supply) as at the end of the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Fuel Supply Access KPI. This is a country-level characteristic, not a description of the utility's individual supply contracts.

The country's gross domestic product divided by its population, expressed in currency per person. Use the latest official figure for the report's fiscal year from the national statistics office, central bank, or ministry of finance national accounts. Feeds the GDP per Capita KPI. Enter the value in the utility's local currency; PRISM converts to USD using the USD Exchange Rate input, so do not pre-convert.

The total number of households in the country, expressed as a count of households. Use the latest official national figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, updated to the report's fiscal year where an official projection is available. Feeds the Households KPI. Report the national total, not the number of households in the utility's service area and not the utility's customer count, which can differ substantially.

The country's air connectivity score as published by the International Air Transport Association (IATA), expressed as a percentage. Use the most recent IATA score available for the report's fiscal year; where the national statistics office or civil aviation authority republishes the figure, confirm it matches the IATA source. Feeds the IATA Air Connectivity Score KPI. Do not substitute a locally derived connectivity measure for the IATA-published score.

The country's annual rate of consumer price inflation for the reporting year, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or central bank for the report's fiscal year; deflation is entered as a negative value. Feeds the Inflation Rate KPI. Take care to match the utility's fiscal year rather than defaulting to the calendar-year figure where the two differ.

The total number of islands making up the country, expressed as a count of islands. Use the official figure published by the national statistics office or national mapping authority, including uninhabited islands where that is the basis of the official count. Feeds the Islands KPI. Record the national total, not only the islands served by the utility.

The total land area of the country, expressed in square kilometres (km2). Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or national mapping authority, covering land area only and excluding territorial waters and exclusive economic zone. Feeds the Land Area KPI. A common error is reporting the EEZ or total maritime area, which for Pacific island countries is vastly larger than the land area.

The total resident population of the country, expressed in persons. Use the latest official national figure from the national statistics office, based on the most recent census or the official mid-year estimate for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Population KPI. Report the national population, not the population of the utility's service area, which may cover only some islands or urban centres.

The share of the country's population living in rural areas, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, applying the national statistical definition of rural areas for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Rural Population KPI. Check that the rural and urban population shares entered are consistent and together account for the whole population.

The country's unemployment rate for the reporting year, expressed as the percentage of the labour force that is unemployed. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office, typically from the labour force survey or census, for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Unemployment Rate KPI. Note that survey-based rates can differ from registered-unemployment counts; use the official labour force survey definition where available.

The share of the country's population living in urban areas, expressed as a percentage. Use the latest official figure from the national statistics office or the most recent census, applying the national statistical definition of urban areas for the report's fiscal year. Feeds the Urban Population KPI. Check that the urban and rural population shares entered are consistent and together account for the whole population.

A descriptive selection identifying the accounting standards under which the utility prepares its financial statements, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the standard actually applied in the utility's audited financial statements for the reporting year (for example IFRS or a national standard), as stated in the accounting policies note of the annual report. Feeds the Accounting Standards KPI. If the utility changed standards during the year, report the standard applied to the year-end financial statements.

A descriptive selection identifying how the utility's electricity business is regulated, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the regulatory arrangement applying to the utility during the reporting year, for example oversight by an independent regulator, regulation by a government ministry, or self-regulation. Feeds the Electricity Regulation KPI. Report the arrangement that actually governs the utility's tariffs and service standards, not simply what legislation provides for on paper.

A descriptive selection identifying the type of feeders that characterise the utility's distribution network, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the option that best describes the utility's network configuration (for example predominantly overhead, underground, or mixed) as at the end of the reporting year. Feeds the Feeder Type KPI. Where the network is mixed, choose the option representing the predominant arrangement rather than the ideal or planned configuration.

A descriptive selection identifying the power quality standards the utility operates to, chosen from the managed list of options provided in PRISM. Select the standard formally applied to the utility's supply voltage and frequency performance during the reporting year, whether set by legislation, the regulator, or the utility's own adopted standard. Feeds the Power Quality Standards KPI. Report the standard actually in force for the utility, not aspirational standards under consideration.

The total cost incurred by the utility during the reporting year to purchase electricity from third parties, such as independent power producers (IPPs), expressed in currency. Include all amounts payable under power purchase agreements and other bulk electricity purchases for the fiscal year, and exclude the cost of fuel used in the utility's own generation. Feeds the Power Purchase Costs KPI. Enter the value in the utility's local currency for the utility's fiscal year; leave blank only if the utility purchases no power from third parties.

The exchange rate between the utility's local currency and the United States dollar for the reporting year, expressed as the number of local currency units per one US dollar. Use the official rate published by the central bank or national statistics office for the utility's fiscal year, applied consistently from year to year. This rate is used to convert all local-currency financial inputs to USD for cross-utility comparison in the PPA Benchmarking Report, and feeds the USD Exchange Rate KPI. A common error is entering the rate inverted (USD per local unit) or using a spot rate inconsistent with the fiscal year being reported.
synonyms: foreign exchange rate to US dollar

definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Annual Report discloses actual performance against the objectives and targets set in its Strategic Plan. Answer "Yes" only if the published Annual Report for the reporting year explicitly compares achieved results with the goals or targets of the adopted Strategic Plan, not merely if both documents exist separately. Feeds the Does the Annual Report disclose performance relative to the Strategic Plan KPI. General narrative about achievements without reference to the plan's targets does not qualify as a "Yes".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the financial statements in the utility's Annual Report are independently audited. Answer "Yes" only if the financial statements for the reporting year have been audited by an independent external auditor, such as a registered audit firm or the national audit office, and an audit opinion has been issued. Feeds the Is the Annual Report audited KPI. An internal audit review or an audit still in progress at the time of reporting does not qualify as a "Yes".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Annual Report is completed within four months of the end of the reporting year. Answer "Yes" only if the Annual Report for the reporting year was finalised, including audited financial statements, within four months of the utility's fiscal year end. Feeds the Is the Annual Report completed within four months of the end of the reporting year KPI. Measure the four months from the utility's own fiscal year end, not the calendar year end, and use the completion date rather than the date of tabling in parliament.

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Code of Conduct is actively implemented, as distinct from merely existing. Answer "Yes" only if the code is applied in practice during the reporting year — for example staff are made aware of it and acknowledge it, training or induction covers it, and breaches are acted upon. Feeds the Is a Code of Conduct implemented KPI. A code that has been adopted but is not communicated or enforced should be answered "No" here even if "Is a Code of Conduct in place?" is answered "Yes".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has a formally adopted Code of Conduct. Answer "Yes" only if a written code of conduct or code of ethics covering directors and/or staff has been formally approved by the Board or management and was current during the reporting year. Feeds the Is a Code of Conduct in place KPI. A draft code, or general provisions scattered across HR policies without a formally adopted code, should be answered "No".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's commercial mandate is followed in practice, as distinct from merely existing in its founding documents. Answer "Yes" only if, during the reporting year, the utility actually operated on commercial principles — for example pursuing cost recovery, being managed to financial performance targets, and having non-commercial obligations identified and treated separately. Feeds the Is a Commercial mandate implemented KPI. A utility whose legislation requires commercial operation but which is run to non-commercial directives in practice should answer "No" here.

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has a formal commercial mandate. Answer "Yes" only if the utility's establishing legislation, charter, articles, or state-owned-enterprise framework formally requires it to operate as a commercial business, for example to be financially self-sustaining or to earn a commercial return. Feeds the Is a Commercial mandate in place KPI. This item concerns the formal mandate only; whether the mandate is actually followed is captured by the separate "Is a Commercial Mandate implemented?" item.

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether serving government ministers are appointed as members of the utility's Board of Directors. Answer "Yes" only if one or more persons holding ministerial office sat on the Board at any time during the reporting year. Feeds the Are Ministers appointed to the Board KPI. The question concerns ministers themselves, not civil servants or ministry officials appointed as government representatives, and not ministers acting solely as shareholders.

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the CEO's performance contract provides for annual performance reviews. Answer "Yes" only if the contract requires the Board (or responsible authority) to formally review the CEO's performance against the contract's targets at least once a year, and such a review was conducted for the reporting year. Feeds the Does the CEOs performance contract include annual reviews KPI. Informal or ad hoc discussions of performance without a documented annual review process do not qualify as a "Yes".
synonyms: yearly performance assessment of chief executive

definition: A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Chief Executive Officer is employed under a performance contract. Answer "Yes" only if the CEO's contract of employment includes defined, measurable performance targets or key performance indicators against which the CEO is assessed. Feeds the Is the CEO on a performance contract KPI. A standard employment contract without explicit performance targets should be answered "No".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Strategic Plan includes forecasts covering three or more years. Answer "Yes" only if the adopted Strategic Plan contains financial and/or operational forecasts (for example demand, revenue, expenditure, or investment projections) spanning at least three future years. Feeds the Does the Strategic Plan include three or more years of forecasts KPI. A plan stating multi-year objectives but containing only a single-year budget or no quantified forecasts should be answered "No".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility has formally adopted a Strategic Plan. Answer "Yes" only if a written strategic (or corporate) plan setting out the utility's objectives and direction has been formally approved by the Board and was current during the reporting year. Feeds the Has a Strategic Plan been adopted KPI. A plan that is in draft, expired, or awaiting Board approval should be answered "No".

A Yes/No governance questionnaire item recording whether the utility's Strategic Plan is actively implemented, as distinct from merely being adopted. Answer "Yes" only if, during the reporting year, the plan genuinely guided operations — for example its initiatives were resourced and under way, and progress against it was monitored and reported to the Board or management. Feeds the Is the Strategic Plan implemented KPI. A plan that sits on the shelf without linked actions, budgets, or progress reporting should be answered "No" even if formally adopted.
